reason: The text contains multiple regular people characters with lines, emotions, and opinions. Sanballat (סנבלט) hears about the wall, becomes angry (וַיִּחַר לוֹ), and mocks the Jews with rhetorical questions expressing his contempt. Tobiah the Ammonite (טוביה העמוני) is present and adds his own taunting remarks. Nehemiah, as the main narrator, demonstrates emotions (concern, determination) and expresses opinions throughout, giving speeches and commands to the people. The Jewish workers themselves speak, expressing their fears and concerns about enemy threats ('Our enemies say...'). The Arabs, Ammonites, and Ashdodites display emotional reactions (anger: וַיִּחַר לָהֶם מְאֹד) and express intentions. All these characters have direct speech, emotional reactions, and articulated viewpoints woven throughout the narrative.
